title: There were many seats specifically for Deaf, HOH and ASL community au...
transcript: Join me at the theater Tonight I'm seeing Deaf Broadway's production of Rent at Lincoln Center I have never seen a more beautiful production of Rent in my entire life Deaf Broadway was started in 2020 as a way to make America's most iconic theatrical shows fully accessible and enjoyable for Deaf, Hard of Hearing and ASL audiences in a way that many of these shows have never been before I truly did not know what to expect I honestly thought they were going to be doing songs from Rent with ASL interpretation. No. This was the full show! There was a small set, some costumes, think like New York City Center Encores. With full out performances, full out staging. The show was captioned and signed during all of the book scenes and then when there was singing which let’s be real it's Rent so it's almost all sung through. They played the Orginal Broadway cast recording under it and then interpreted but I was so mesmerized by the performances that I forgot that no one was singing live. I was on the floor when they were signing for La Vie Bohème and like the signing was so beautiful and funny and fast. The entire cast was so good Anjel Piñero’s Mimi brought the house down Maureen was Sandra Mae Frank who might be my favorite Maureen of all time and then John McGinty and James Caverly were Roger and Mark and they're just legendary. This was a one night only performance and I don't know how. I need someone to produce this immediately. It needs to be seen by more people and we need to be doing more theater in this way so many people around me had literally never seen Rent before and I loved watching them experience the show this was part of Lincoln Center's American Songbook series They produced events like this that are free and ‘pay what you want’ all year long which is so cool and finally as always thank you Jonathan Larson
